clusters.title: NewRouter registers POST /setTasks, POST /tasks, GET/DELETE /tasks/{id} and GET /health with no auth middleware (router.go:21-32). createTask/syncTasks decode an attacker-controlled JSON body requiring only a non-empty Name; Command/Args/Env/WorkingDir/ExecMode flow unchanged (handler.go:56-131). The executor concatenates Command+Args and runs them via /bin/sh -c (process.go:88-134); ExecMode=Remote selects the nsenter branch (process.go:111-128), and findPidByEnvVar picks the first /proc/*/environ process containing SANDBOX_MAIN_CONTAINER=<value> with no ownership checks. The controller client uses plain HTTP with no token (client.go) and the scheduler targets http://<podIP>:5758 (default_scheduler.go:157-166). Samples launch task-executor with -listen-addr=0.0.0.0:5758 and the image is built with USERID=0 (Makefile:259). No NetworkPolicy covers 5758. execd bwrap isolation defaults ShareNet=true (isolated_session.go:203) so it does not unshare net (bwrap.go:197), leaving 127.0.0.1:5758 reachable from isolated user sessions. This is an authorization gap, not shell injection: shellEscape mitigates argument injection, but any caller may choose the command. HYP-001 adds that maxConcurrentTasks=1 lets an unauthenticated caller occupy the only slot and block controller task delivery (task_manager.go:34,114-116,296-298).

clusters.title: findPidByEnvVar scans /proc/*/environ and returns the first PID whose environment contains SANDBOX_MAIN_CONTAINER=<MainContainerName>, skipping only its own PID; there is no ownership, UID, cgroup or container-identity check (process.go:576-620). It then reads that environment and nsenter's all namespaces (111-128). With PID-namespace sharing a co-tenant process could race to be selected and influence the environment/namespaces. Without sharing, the target is likely limited to the same container; not confirmed against a default deployment.

clusters.title: websocket.Accept is called with InsecureSkipVerify: true, bypassing same-origin checks (websocket.go:155-162); the comment assumes a trusted upstream gateway enforces this. Client X-Forwarded-For is appended rather than replaced (258-261), and the plain HTTP path trusts the first XFF hop (proxy.go:486-490). If the ingress is exposed, any site can open a WebSocket and spoof source addresses; backends must not trust these headers.
